members.name: significance
members.doc:
Significance: when the emitter budget (r.Effects max active emitters,
overdraw budget) bites, emitters are admitted by significance — this
priority over distance — instead of nearest-first, so a far muzzle
flash outranks near ambient dust. Always Relevant bypasses the budget
entirely (the one effect a gameplay beat must not lose).

members.name: particlePath
members.doc:
Linked .particle asset. The `modules` vector below is runtime-only, so
without this scene-authored module sets were lost on save/load. Scene
deserialize re-clones the asset's modules onto the emitter (see
Scene::DeserializeFromDocument), making authored particles persist.

members.name: seed
members.doc:
Zero means "seed from the platform entropy source at pool init", i.e.
a different effect every run. Any non-zero value makes the emitter
reproducible across runs, machines and networked clients.

members.name: simulationMode
members.doc: Simulation mode handled by the custom (de)serialize hooks above.

members.name: renderMode
members.doc:
Billboard quads (default) or an instanced mesh per particle. Mesh mode
submits through the scene's static-mesh path, so mesh particles are
deferred-lit by the whole scene without a lit toggle.

members.name: meshPath
members.doc:
Mesh-mode source. A model asset ref wins; otherwise the primitive named
by meshType is used (cube/sphere/cylinder/cone/capsule/torus/plane/quad),
mirroring the MeshRenderer resolution contract.

members.name: shadingMode
members.doc:
Billboard shading. Unlit keeps the classic emissive look; Lit runs a
simplified forward loop (main directional N·L + ambient/GI) so smoke and
dust sit in the scene's lighting. Mesh mode is always deferred-lit.

members.name: velocityStretch
members.doc:
Stretched billboard tuning. The quad's long axis aligns with the
particle velocity and its length grows with speed:
stretch = clamp(1 + speed * velocityStretch, 1, stretchMax). Only used
when billboardMode is Stretched.

members.name: subUVColumns
members.doc:
Flipbook grid over the particle texture; the frame is picked from the
particle's normalized age and baked into the quad UVs at submission.

members.name: softFadeDistance
members.doc:
World-space distance over which a particle fades out as it approaches

types.name: ParticleCollisionMode
types.doc:
Which scene representation a collision module resolves against.

Auto takes the best tier the frame's field offers. The two are not
equivalent: the world distance field covers geometry the camera cannot see,
so a particle behind a wall or off the side of the screen still lands on
something. The depth buffer only knows what was rasterized this frame, so a
particle that leaves the view stops colliding and one behind an occluder
collides against the occluder's front face. Depth is the cheap fallback for
tiers that do not build the distance field.

types.name: ParticleCollisionField
types.doc:
One frame's view of the scene as something particles can hit.

Both representations live above this module — the distance field belongs to
the renderer's clipmap and the depth pyramid to its occlusion path — so the
simulation only ever sees this sampling contract. A null field means no
collision is available and collision modules pass their particles through
untouched.

members.name: SampleSdf
members.signature: virtual bool SampleSdf(const Vec3& worldPos, float& outDistance, Vec3& outNormal) const = 0
members.doc:
Signed distance from worldPos to the nearest surface and the surface's
outward normal (the normalized field gradient). Negative distance means
the point is inside geometry. Returns false outside the field's window.

members.name: SampleDepth
members.signature: virtual bool SampleDepth(const Vec3& worldPos, float& outPenetration, Vec3& outNormal) const = 0
members.doc:
Depth tier: how far worldPos sits behind the rasterized surface covering
its pixel, plus that surface's normal reconstructed from neighbouring
depth texels. outPenetration is positive when the point is behind the
surface. Returns false when the point is off-screen or behind the camera.

types.name: FParticleExpression
types.doc:
A per-particle script, the Niagara scratch-pad analogue: statements of the
form `vel.y = vel.y - 9.8 * dt` (also += -= *= /=), separated by newlines or
semicolons, compiled once into stack bytecode and run for every particle —
on the CPU by Run, on the GPU by Particles/GPUParticleExpression.comp.hlsl,
which interprets the same bytecode (AppendGpuProgram packs it).

Writable: pos.x/y/z, vel.x/y/z, size.x/y, rot, spin, col.r/g/b/a, life, and
up to four custom attributes `attr.<name>` that live on the particle for its
whole life (zero at spawn). Read-only: age, nage (0..1), dt, time,
emitter.x/y/z, param1..param4, pi, rand (a fresh uniform [0,1) per read).
Any other name assigned before it is read is a local. Functions: sin cos tan
abs sign floor frac sqrt exp min max pow atan2 mod step clamp lerp
smoothstep. Operators: + - * / < > <= >= == != && || ! and the ternary
`c ? a : b`.

types.name: LightModule
types.doc:
Light module - the emitter's brightest particles become dynamic point
lights that illuminate the scene. The module owns no per-particle state; it
is a budgeted marker the renderer reads (see Scene::SubmitParticleLights) so
sparks, embers and muzzle flashes light the walls around them.

members.name: color
members.doc: Emitted colour. Multiplied by the particle's own colour when tintFromParticle.

members.name: intensity

members.name: radius

members.name: maxLights
members.doc:
How many of the emitter's particles may be lights in one frame. The
brightest/largest are chosen first so a dense spark burst still lights
the scene without spawning thousands of lights.

members.name: fadeWithLifetime
members.doc:
Fraction of each light's intensity scaled by the particle's normalized
remaining life, so a dying ember fades its light out with it.

members.name: tintFromParticle
members.doc:
Multiply the emitted colour by the particle's current colour, so a
colour-graded spark tints the light it casts.

or every update, where the fixed modules run out — a spiral, a colour that
follows speed, a size pulse. A spawn script runs on the CPU for both
simulation modes (GPU particles are spawned by the CPU); an update script on
a GPU emitter runs in the GPU expression pass, on the same bytecode.

types.name: SubEmitterModule
types.doc:
Sub-emitter: wherever the parent's particles are born, die or hit something,
spawn particles into a child emitter — sparks that burst into embers on
impact, a firework shell that dies into a shower. The child is either
another emitter of the same .vfx system, named by childEmitter, or an asset
of its own, childPath. It is resolved into the parent's children and spawns
only from these events.

members.doc: Particles spawned into the child per event.

members.name: probability
members.doc: Chance each event fires at all, so a dense parent can seed a sparse child.

members.name: inheritVelocity
members.doc: Share of the parent particle's velocity added to the child's own.

members.name: inheritColor
members.doc: Multiply the child's start colour by the parent particle's colour.

members.name: maxEventsPerFrame
members.doc:
Cap on events handled per frame, so a mass death cannot spawn an
unbounded burst.

members.name: childSlot
members.doc:
Index into the owning emitter's children, set when the scene resolves
the emitter; -1 until then (the module does nothing).

members.doc:
Scene representation collision modules resolve against. Owned by the
caller and expected to stay valid for the frame; null disables
collision without disabling the modules.

members.name: WantsDepthCollision
members.doc:
True when at least one live emitter carries a collision module that can
use the depth tier. The renderer reads this to decide whether the
depth downsample and its readback are worth running at all — nothing
pays for depth collision in a scene that does not ask for it.

members.name: WantsSdfCollision
members.doc:
True when a live CPU emitter carries a collision module that can sample
the distance field, as of the last tick. The host only asks the renderer
for its CPU copy of the field while this holds.

members.name: BakeGPUSimParams
members.signature: void BakeGPUSimParams(const struct ParticleEmitterComponent& emitter, const Vec3& emitterPos, GPUParticleSimParams& params) const
members.doc:
Bake an emitter's modules into GPU sim params (public so the collision
parity self-test can assert the baked CollisionModule values without a GPU).

members.name: GetCollisionCount
members.doc: Contacts resolved across every emitter on the last Update.

members.name: SetViewportSize
members.doc:
Backbuffer size, used to turn a world-space particle quad into an
estimated pixel count for the fill budget. Zero disables the estimate.

members.name: SetOverdrawBudget
members.doc:
Fill budget. Particle cost is overdraw, not simulation, so the budget is
denominated in screen coverage: an emitter's estimated covered pixels
(quad areas summed, overlaps counted twice — that IS the overdraw) over
the backbuffer's pixel count. A budget of 2 means "particles may cover
the screen twice over". Emitters are admitted nearest-first and the
first one that would blow the budget, and everything behind it, is
dropped for the frame. Zero means unlimited.

members.name: GetEstimatedOverdraw
members.doc:
Estimated screens of fill the last SubmitForRendering actually admitted,
and how many emitters the budget rejected.

members.name: SetVisibilityFilter
members.doc:
Per-view visibility veto, rebound alongside the camera. Particles gather
out of the World directly, so without this the scene's own layer mask and
editor-hidden filter stop at every other renderable and let emitters
through. Empty = submit everything, which is what a host with no scene
(the standalone emitter tests) wants.

spawn rate, pool size and cull distance. 1.0 leaves content untouched.

uses (the SDF volume + depth textures are bound by the renderer).

settings). This mirrors the fields a property-authored ParticleAsset carries,
so a graph-compiled config and a property-authored one are directly

"Rotation", "Collision", "Light"). Params carries the node's serialized
